Content: On Christmas Eve in `1979`, the Soviet Union invaded Afghanistan to rescue a Communist-leaning government under attack by Islamic rebels. These rebels were known as mujahedeen, or “holy warriors.” To hurt its Cold War foe, the U.S. began arming the mujahedeen in the `text(1980s)`. This helped the rebels secure a stalemate against the Soviet army, which finally pulled out its troops in `1989`. With the Soviets gone, factions of mujahedeen battled each other. By `1996`, the Taliban, a radical Islamist group, controlled the country. . . .
